analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) Asia FX Update, 2) BRL Colour, 3) AI Outlook Podcast and 4) 5 Key Charts 20 Nov 2026
key_insights: Asia FX desk (Sun Lu, EM Market Strats) describes a significant risk-off. INR is the only clear long in the region, helped by lower oil and AI de-risking.

INR: real money accounts still have a decent underweight in Indian equities to cover. The RBI's USD windows to oil marketing companies are still roughly US$10bn/month of USD selling. Flows skew positive and the market is surprised the RBI has not started meaningful USD buying. Any USDINR rebound is seen as an opportunity for the INR carry trade.

CNY: the fix has provided stability after APEC on goodwill, though nothing substantial came out of it. Spot was volatile over the past 24 hours. GS expects fixing-driven CNY appreciation over the next few months and continues to like short USDCNY NDF.

TWD and THB: both are suspected to have seen strong defence in recent days despite a Taiwan equity selloff and large equity outflows. USDTWD 33 has not broken for over a week and USDTHB 34 has not broken despite sharp gold weakness. If those levels hold, GS expects tactical strength in TWD (if tech equity recovers) and THB (on tourism seasonality).

KRW: in a range, with equity outflows offset by exporter flows. GS flow math says FX stays skewed to USD selling if daily foreign equity outflow is under US$500mn. USDKRW may rebound into the Nov 27 Samsung KRW30tn dividend payment (est. US$8bn outflow to foreigners), and such rebounds could be opportunities for USDKRW downside.

BRL: Brazilian assets sold off heavily with a sharp bear flattening in rates. DI Jan29 sold off as much as 50bp intraday and implied Selic reached 16%. The front end is about 40bp wider and spreads flattened roughly 5-15bp. USDBRL traded above 5.95, about 1.3% higher on the day, with the BCB selling US$1bn spot.

BRL drivers: fiscal and political uncertainty, including news that Planning Minister Bruno Moretti was gaining traction as a potential Finance Minister, plus global risk-off in US equities and EM FX. The sell-off accelerated after the BCB intervened in FX and rates initially priced the operation as rate hikes. Offshore stops added momentum.

BRL positioning amplified the move. The market was concentrated in front-end receivers and steepeners, and DIs had outperformed the BRL sell-off over the previous sessions, leaving room for rates to catch up once stops triggered.

BRL view: despite similarities with 2024, GS sees virtually no room for the BCB to hike to re-anchor markets given an expected material economic slowdown. It favours front-end receivers and would add on further sell-offs, while noting the near-term environment is very difficult given fiscal uncertainty, a potentially lengthy Finance Ministry nomination process and unclear upcoming BCB board appointments.

Podcast: Tony Pasquariello (GS Global Head of Hedge Fund Coverage) and Jim Schneider (GIR, US Semiconductors and IT Services) discuss NVDA earnings takeaways, financing and power supply constraints, and market expectations for 2027 and 2028 capex.

Five key charts flagged: Japan core CPI expected to rise sharply in early 2027 on reduced energy subsidies, improved S&P 500 breadth, Asian equities at a large valuation discount to the US and Europe, CEE-3 headline inflation expected to decline in 2027 on energy base effects, and narrowing US-Mexico rate differentials for MXN.
earnings_insights: NVDA earnings are discussed in the podcast (financing and power supply constraints, 2027 and 2028 capex expectations). The text gives no figures.

tension_points.bull_case: GS favours front-end receivers because a material economic slowdown leaves virtually no room for the BCB to hike.
tension_points.bear_case: Fiscal uncertainty, a lengthy Finance Ministry nomination process and unclear BCB board appointments make the near term very difficult, and the market had rates pricing hikes after the BCB FX intervention.
